entries.finding_title: Event frame is not ready when the webhook arrives (`416`)
entries.finding: `human`: 14 of 20 frames on the first request, ready after the event p50 2.3 s, p90 3.6 s, max 9.8 s. `motion`: 0 of 17 on the first request, always ready on a retry at +2 s or +5 s (p50 3.5 s, p90 6.3 s, max 6.6 s). One `human` event (10-07 21:05Z) answered `416` through +5.9 s.
entries.workaround: retry at receipt +0/2/5/8/12/16/20 s (`PROBE_OFFSETS_MS`, `src/frames.ts`); a 200 counts only if it is a `recording` within 1 s of the event and not after receipt (`checkEventFrame`).

entries.finding_title: `other_motion` webhooks arrive about 11 s late and their recording is later still
entries.endpoint: webhook `motion_detected` with `sub_type: other_motion`; media download as in F-01.
entries.finding: `received_after_event_ms` 10724 and 11211; webhook delay p50 10.9 s for `other_motion` against 1.2 s for `human`. The recording was `416` at receipt +5 s and +10 s and `200` at +15 s, so about 21 to 26 s after the event. On 10-07 23:12Z every request through event +30.9 s was `416`; 1 of 4 `other_motion` events got a frame.
entries.workaround: retries run to receipt +20 s; wildlife frames may be up to 35 s old (`wildlifeMaxEvidenceAgeMs`, ceiling 40 s) while the intruder ladder keeps its 15 s rule.

entries.finding_title: `latest_in_range` returns the end of the window, not the event
entries.observed: 10-07 13:33 CDT, over the 30 s after an event.
entries.finding: frames came back 10.8 s and 29.9 s after the event.
entries.workaround: use `at_timestamp` with the webhook's `attributes.timestamp`; the result carries `X-Media-Timestamp`, which we treat as the capture time.

entries.finding: a 24 h window was refused with "Requested time range is not within authorized boundaries"; a window starting 16:31:35 (the link time) was accepted. The code is not in `api-documentation.html`. The exact boundary was not bisected.
entries.workaround: request windows that start at or after link time.

entries.finding_title: Recordings end 10 to 14 s after the event
entries.endpoint: `POST /v1/devices/{id}/media/image/download`, `at_timestamp` at `now - 2 s` (follow-up probe at receipt +5/+10/+15 s).
entries.finding: `human` (camera 1): 54 of 54 `200` at event +4 s and +9 s. At event +14 s the frame returned is earlier than requested in 12 of 18 `human` and 15 of 16 `motion` events, by up to 4.1 s.
entries.workaround: live view as the freshness source (in progress); Plan B is L1 plus voice on clip evidence with the ledger saying `source clip`.

entries.finding_title: Webhook delivery lag has a long tail
entries.observed: from the link (10-06 16:31 CDT) to 10-07 13:17 CDT, n = 65.
entries.finding: from `attributes.timestamp` to receipt: min 708 ms, p50 1079 ms, p90 1335 ms, max 30720 ms.
entries.workaround: the ledger records Ring capture time and the age of every frame, so a late webhook shows as an older frame, never as a fresher one.
entries.reproduce: `jq -r '(.received_at | sub("\\.[0-9]+Z$";"Z") | fromdate) - (.body.data.attributes.timestamp / 1000)' webhook-events.jsonl | sort -n` (whole seconds, from the webhook log).

entries.observed: no Ring webhooks from 10-08 00:00Z to 15:00Z (19:00 to 10:00 CDT).
entries.finding: the probe has no night samples for that span. Cause not checked: Ring motion schedule or mode, no motion, or a delivery failure.
entries.workaround: none. A quiet night and a dead webhook look the same in the ledger today.
entries.reproduce: `jq -r '.received_at[0:13]' webhook-events.jsonl | sort | uniq -c` (webhooks per hour, UTC).

entries.finding_title: The account-link flow starts in the Ring AppStore, not in the console
entries.finding: the console button only authorizes an account to see the private app and sends nothing to our endpoints; the journal stayed empty until the AppStore approval at 16:28:42 CDT on 10-06. The token-exchange POST carries exactly `code` and `client_id`; the docs do not name the field.
entries.workaround: `extractCode` accepts the likely spellings; the flow is written down in `docs/recon.md`.
entries.reproduce: `docs/recon.md`, "Linking is started from the Ring AppStore".

entries.finding_title: Device encryption (TAKE and E2EE) can make video unreadable while requests still succeed
entries.observed: instrumented 2026-10-11 (`src/encryption.ts`); not yet measured on our cameras.
entries.request_id: recorded in `friction.jsonl` once the build runs.
entries.finding: Ring documents that for an encrypted device video requests succeed and return content the app cannot read. The configurations response is the only place the flag appears in the documentation read; it is not in the `include=configurations` table.
entries.workaround: the service reads the flag at startup and every 30 minutes; an encrypted camera gets no frame request and its events are ledger lines marked `blind: camera video is encrypted`. A frame that is not JPEG bytes is refused as `not_jpeg_bytes` even when the flag could not be read. The Playground sandbox switch is not built: its base URL and token flow are not in `api-documentation.html`.
entries.reproduce: `test/encryption.test.ts` for the logic; on the real service, `grep e2e_encryption friction.jsonl` once the build has run.

entries.finding_title: Every image carries a Ring watermark
entries.finding: the watermark holds a device ID suffix, "Partner: Quiet Porch" and the generation time.
entries.reproduce: `docs/recon.md`, "Stored image download"; any frame saved to `~/.local/state/quiet-porch/frames/`.

entries.finding_title: Sandbox and Playground details are missing from the API documentation
entries.observed: 2026-10-11, `api-documentation.html` read in full for `e2e_encryption`, TAKE and Playground.
entries.finding: the page lists one API host, `https://api.amazonvision.com`, and no sandbox host or sandbox token flow; "TAKE" appears only as a link to the developer FAQ.
entries.workaround: none in code. How to reach the Playground is not in the documentation read, so the sandbox switch in F-09 is blocked on that answer.
entries.reproduce: open `api-documentation.html` and search for `sandbox`, `Playground`, `TAKE`; only the production host and a FAQ link turn up.

entries.finding_title: JSON comes back inside a code fence
entries.observed: 10-06 (gate), recorded in `docs/recon.md`; the parser has handled the fence on every call since without a logged failure.
entries.request_id: not captured before 2026-10-11; `model-calls.jsonl` from then on.
entries.finding: with "Return ONLY a JSON object" in the prompt the model still wraps it in a json code fence. First call: `200` in 2428 ms, 378 input and 69 output tokens.
entries.workaround: `parseModelJson` strips one fenced block and fails closed on anything else (prose around the object); a parse failure closes the event at L0 as "perception failed".

entries.finding_title: Two model calls per person event put the decision 8 to 12 s after the event
entries.finding: frames are ready 1.8 s to 6.3 s after the event and decisions land 8 to 12 s after it; two calls take about 6 s.
entries.workaround: the second call runs only when a person or a configured nuisance species was seen (`needsCritique`).

entries.finding_title: Not yet tested against a real Alexa+ device
entries.endpoint: `quiet-porch-status` MCP server, Streamable HTTP, specification 2025-11-25, tools only, single JSON responses, no SSE stream.
entries.observed: curl and a browser against the simulated page at `/alexa` on 10-07; the ledger tools (`get_night_report`, `get_ledger`, `expect_me`) added 2026-10-11.
entries.finding: protocol behaviour (initialize, `tools/list`, 401 without a token, 405 on GET, Origin check) is covered by `test/mcp.test.ts` and `test/mcp-night.test.ts`. No real Echo or Alexa+ client has called the server, so friction on that side is unmeasured.
entries.workaround: the simulated page maps spoken phrases to the same tools.

entries.endpoint: Polly generative voices (voice ID to be chosen on day one of the voice work).
entries.finding: nothing measured. The line composer and banned-word filter (`src/voice.ts`) exist behind a stub; the Polly call and its latency (target under 3 s, cached fallback phrase) are not built yet.
entries.reproduce: `npx vitest run test/voice.test.ts` covers the composer only.
